payload.title: Amsterdam Avenue
payload.subtitle: A protected route, from a board vote to a completed corridor.
payload.subject: West 72nd → West 110th Street
payload.summary: CB7 supported a complete-street design. DOT later named the same stretch of Amsterdam Avenue among its completed 2016 projects.
payload.match: Reviewed corridor match: Amsterdam Avenue, West 72nd–West 110th, protected bicycle lane, NYC DOT. The board supported an agency proposal already in development; the records do not prove the vote caused construction.
limits: The documented result is installation, not proof that every requested condition was met.
No independent field inspection or current-condition survey is included.
payload.next_action: Find the task-force records or later corridor evaluation before marking the evaluation request fulfilled.

payload.title: The full board supports the project
payload.summary: CB7 adopted support for the redesign, while also requesting outreach and continuing evaluation.
payload.result_basis: Full-board vote on the named resolution. The separate committee tally is not substituted.

payload.title: DOT presents the design
payload.summary: DOT presented a protected northbound lane and scheduled Phase 1 from West 72nd to West 110th for spring implementation. This was a plan, not evidence of completion.

payload.title: DOT reports the corridor completed
payload.summary: A dated DOT announcement lists Amsterdam Avenue from West 72nd to West 110th among projects completed in 2016. The announcement date is not the construction completion date.

payload.text: Build the protected lane on the named corridor

payload.note: Board and agency records identify the same street and endpoints.

payload.text: Establish the proposed neighborhood evaluation task force

payload.note: The resolution requests it; the selected completion record does not establish that it formed.

payload.title: Chrystie Street
payload.subtitle: A community request, a revised design, a finished connection.
payload.subject: Houston → Canal Street
payload.summary: The record connects a request for safety improvements to DOT’s design, a full-board endorsement and a later completion announcement.
payload.match: Reviewed project match: Chrystie Street protected bicycle lane, Houston–Canal corridor and NYC DOT. The agency design and board record identify the same intervention; the completion release names the facility.
limits: The original February 2015 resolution is represented only through the May 2016 retrospective account.
Construction completion is documented; causal impact and fulfillment of every design detail are not evaluated.
payload.next_action: Pair the completed design with a later corridor safety evaluation if the next question is whether it improved safety.

payload.title: The board requests safety improvements
payload.summary: The May 2016 minutes recount a February 2015 board resolution seeking safety improvements. This is a retrospective account; the original February resolution was not separately reviewed.
payload.basis: Earlier event reported in later board minutes

payload.title: DOT brings a two-way protected-lane design
payload.summary: DOT’s presentation identifies the board’s request for a study and proposes separation from traffic.

payload.title: Stakeholders review the design
payload.summary: The May minutes report an April 13 DOT workshop and say local input was incorporated. This is the board’s account of the workshop.
payload.basis: Workshop reported in later board minutes

payload.title: The full board supports the final plan
payload.summary: CB3 supports DOT’s protected-lane plan following the reported workshop. The adopted Transportation vote includes this item.
payload.result_basis: Transportation item 3 is covered by the omnibus vote excluding item 6. The separate item 6 tally is not used.

payload.title: DOT announces the lane is complete
payload.summary: DOT’s announcement confirms completion of the Chrystie protected lane. It does not establish a measured safety effect caused by the board’s resolution.

payload.note: The named facility is supported in the minutes and confirmed by DOT.

payload.text: Seek local input before the final design

payload.note: The board’s own account records the April workshop and incorporation of input; not an independent workshop audit.

payload.title: Columbus Avenue
payload.subtitle: The follow-up comes back to the board.
payload.subject: West 96th → West 77th Street
payload.summary: A full-board vote is followed by an installation update, a return presentation and DOT’s retrospective confirmation of the original segment.
payload.match: Reviewed exact-segment match: Columbus Avenue, West 96th–West 77th. The 2012 slides distinguish the already installed 2010 segment from proposed extensions, preventing a later phase from being mistaken for the original outcome.
limits: 2012 is the date of confirmation in the selected DOT document, not the year construction finished.

The accepted six-month evaluation and publication condition is distinct from the rejected amendment that would have required CB7 participation in decisions to revisit, end, expand, modify or make the lane permanent.
The October 2011 return presentation does not by itself establish timely compliance with the accepted six-month condition or publication to the community.
payload.next_action: Locate a dated six-month evaluation and evidence that its results were published to CB7 and the community; the October 2011 presentation alone does not close that condition.

payload.title: The full board approves installation
payload.summary: CB7 adopts the protected-lane proposal between West 96th and West 77th with a friendly amendment requiring evaluation after six months and publication of results to CB7 and the community. A later amendment seeking CB7 control over whether to revisit, end, expand, modify or make the lane permanent failed.
payload.result_basis: Final adopted motion on PDF page 9. The accepted friendly amendment requiring a six-month evaluation and publication of results is included; the later failed amendment seeking CB7 control over future changes is excluded.

payload.title: An installation update reaches the cabinet
payload.summary: The cabinet minutes record that the northern section is in use and the remainder is expected after resurfacing. A forecast is not counted as proof of full completion.

payload.title: DOT returns with a post-installation review
payload.summary: Committee minutes record DOT presenting after-data and discussing installed features and ongoing adjustments. This records follow-up; it is not a causal evaluation by this application.

payload.title: DOT confirms the original segment was installed
payload.summary: The presentation’s background explicitly identifies the West 96th–West 77th protected path as installed in 2010. Its later extension proposal is a different scope.

payload.text: Install the protected path between 96th and 77th

payload.note: DOT retrospectively names the exact original segment and installation year.

payload.text: Evaluate after six months and publish results to CB7 and the community

payload.note: A later return presentation is recorded, but the selected evidence does not establish a six-month evaluation or publication of results to both CB7 and the community.

payload.title: St. Marks Place
payload.subtitle: A decision is documented. The later outcome remains open.
payload.subject: Third Avenue → Avenue A
payload.summary: A reviewed public seed records CB3 supporting DOT’s standard bike-lane proposal. This case intentionally has no verified implementation event.
payload.match: Only the decision-to-agency relationship is established in this seed. There is no reviewed later project or implementation link.
limits: This is not a claim that DOT did nothing. It is a gap in the selected evidence.
The source was inherited from a reviewed public CityScroll pilot; the original PDF could not be fetched again.
payload.next_action: Locate a dated DOT response or project update for this exact corridor, then review it before changing the public status.
